boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten recurring Northwest University community practices documented by Student Activities Board and university sources.

cards.title: Welcome Back Bash
cards.subtitle: First day of school outdoor celebration
cards.notes: Start the academic year at SAB’s outdoor gathering, using the lawn games and activities as a low-pressure way to reconnect or meet classmates.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwest University’s Student Activities Board identifies Welcome Back Bash as a campus tradition held on the first day of school.
cards.access_notes: Check SAB’s current event information for date, location, and eligibility.

cards.title: Screaming Eagles Week
cards.subtitle: Living-area competition week
cards.notes: Join your living area for the scheduled challenges, dodgeball tournament, music-video competition, and Eagle Olympics; follow current housing and SAB guidance.
cards.short_summary: A week-long living-area competition with signature challenges.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwest University calls Screaming Eagles Week a venerable custom, and SAB describes its living-area challenges and competitions.
cards.source_title: Charting the Future: Screaming Eagles Week
cards.access_notes: Participation details and event locations vary by year; consult SAB or residence-life announcements.

cards.title: Mr. Northwest
cards.subtitle: Floor-versus-floor satirical pageant
cards.notes: Watch or represent your floor in SAB’s satirical pageant, where living areas compete head-to-head for the Mr. Northwest title.
cards.short_summary: A satirical pageant built around floor competition.
cards.evidence_claim: SAB lists Mr. Northwest among its annual campus traditions and describes it as a satirical male beauty pageant for floors competing head-to-head.
cards.access_notes: Check SAB announcements for the current format, venue, and participation process.

cards.title: Evening
cards.subtitle: End-of-year formal event
cards.notes: Plan ahead for SAB’s end-of-year formal and use the announced venue guidance; past host sites cited by SAB include Seattle cultural institutions.
cards.evidence_claim: SAB identifies Evening as a campus tradition and describes it as an end-of-year formal event.
cards.access_notes: Venue and entry details vary; consult SAB’s current announcement before making plans.

cards.title: Northwest Fest
cards.subtitle: End-of-year food, games, and community
cards.notes: Close the year with the SAB celebration; check the event notice for its food, games, community activities, location, and any attendance details.
cards.evidence_claim: SAB lists Northwest Fest as a recurring campus tradition and describes it as an end-of-year celebration with food trucks, games, and community.
cards.access_notes: Check SAB’s current listing for date, location, and any access requirements.

cards.title: Late-Night Breakfast
cards.subtitle: SAB annual event
cards.notes: Look for the annual Late-Night Breakfast in SAB programming and confirm the current date, food service details, venue, and student access before attending.
cards.short_summary: A named annual SAB gathering centered on breakfast.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwest University’s Pursuit magazine lists Late-Night Breakfast among SAB Annual Events.
cards.access_notes: The cited source confirms it as annual but does not provide current hours; use SAB’s current event notice.

cards.title: Monday Morning Devos
cards.subtitle: Monday chapel-based devotional gathering
cards.notes: Use Monday Morning Devos as a regular start-of-week worship option, and verify the semester’s chapel schedule for the current time and format.
cards.short_summary: A Monday devotional gathering in Northwest’s chapel rhythm.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwest University states that Morning Devos take place on Monday as part of its chapel programming.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current semester schedule and participation expectations with Campus Ministries.

cards.title: Monday Pursuit Worship Nights
cards.subtitle: Monday worship gathering
cards.notes: Attend a Monday Pursuit worship night when it is scheduled, checking Campus Ministries communications for the current location, start time, and format.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwest University states that Pursuit worship nights take place on Monday within its weekly chapel programming.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current semester schedule and participation expectations with Campus Ministries.

cards.title: Weekly Floor Life Groups
cards.subtitle: Residence-hall Bible study practice
cards.notes: Ask your resident assistant about your floor’s weekly life group, then join the scheduled Bible study and conversation with your residence community.
cards.short_summary: A weekly Bible-study practice on every dorm floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwest University states that every dorm floor has a weekly life group where students study the Bible together.
cards.access_notes: Available to residents; ask residence life or your floor’s resident assistant for the current meeting details.

cards.title: The No-Cap-Decorating Commencement
cards.subtitle: Graduation regalia centered on shared community
cards.notes: Graduates should arrive in standard regalia without personal cap or gown decoration, then stay through the ceremony to celebrate the whole graduating community.
cards.short_summary: A commencement practice that prioritizes uniform regalia and collective celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwest University’s 2026 commencement guidance says graduates wear the same regalia, do not decorate caps or gowns, and remain for the entire ceremony.
cards.access_notes: Applies to participating 2026 graduates; follow the university’s current commencement instructions and ticketing requirements.
